newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down after range-bound session.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down after range-bound session.

text.p: Dutch blue chip shares closed mainly down on Thursday after a range-bound day's trading in negative territory, leading dealers to rule out further rises in the AEX index in days to come.
The AEX ended 2.26 points down at 650.08, after a session spent hovering between 644.59 and 652.06 points.
"There was nothing spectacular happening," a dealer said. "Options-led basket trades generated much of the activity."
Exceptions were Philips, still riding high on news it planned to deconsolidate its loss-making Grundig unit, and chemicals firms Akzo and DSM.
Philips topped the volume charts for the entire session, ending 0.20 guilders higher at 72.10, back from a peak of 72.70.
Technically the stock has the potential to rise to its next resistance level of 74-75 guilders, but dealers said gains had been braked by the market downturn.

Akzo and DSM also bucked the blue chip downtrend, building on Wednesday's upbeat earnings message from Akzo chairman Cees van Lede. Akzo gained 1.70 guilders to 248.30, while DSM added 70 cents to 171.30.
Unilever also gained late in the session on demand from U.K. investors, ending 0.50 guilders higher at 300.80, dealers said.
British investors were thought to be switching out of sterling-denominated Unilever stock due to currency worries prompted by the pound's strength.

A lack of fresh Dutch corporate news meant Amsterdam largely tracked surrounding European bourses in low-volume early trade after a softer start on Wall Street's overnight losses and the Nikkei's plunge.
However, opening losses were capped by dollar strength and an early recovery in the Bund future. Dealers said German jobless data had little impact on a generally lacklustre market.
U.S. producer price and jobless claims data released at 1330 GMT occasioned a brief upward flurry on the index, but shares quickly settled back.
A flat Wall Street opening did little to enthuse investors late in the session, although Dutch dealers predicted the Dow Jones would end higher.
"I see us hovering around these levels for the next week or so," one dealer said. Another was more pessimistic: "I foresee a correction of around five percent in the near future."
On Wednesday, traders were still forecasting a steady upward climb on the index.
Confusion on the future direction of the AEX was reflected in the brisk trade in index options.
Options on the AEX accounted for more than a quarter of total options turnover, with calls and puts equally in demand.
